pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word in Bring the clothes inside is the verb? (1 mark)
   A. Bring
   B. the
   C. clothes
   D. inside

2. Where can you check the meaning of a word? (1 mark)
   A. In a simple dictionary
   B. On a clock
   C. On a shoe
   D. In a bag

3. What should you put after a starting word such as First? (1 mark)
   A. A question mark
   B. A colon
   C. A comma
   D. Nothing

4. Which sentence is a metaphor? (1 mark)
   A. The classroom was a beehive.
   B. The classroom was busy.
   C. The classroom was like a beehive.
   D. The classroom was as busy as a beehive.

5. Which sentence is a simile? (1 mark)
   A. She is as bright as the sun.
   B. She is a sun.
   C. She is a shining star.
   D. She is bright.

6. Why do many readers read silently? (1 mark)
   A. It is boring
   B. It is illegal to read aloud
   C. Books cannot be read aloud
   D. It is fast and does not disturb others

7. Why do we explain a proverb in our own words? (1 mark)
   A. To make it longer
   B. To hide it
   C. To show we understand the lesson
   D. To change it forever

8. How should you speak when narrating an event? (1 mark)
   A. Angrily always
   B. Clearly and with feeling
   C. Very quietly
   D. Without stopping

9. What is a good first step when skimming? (1 mark)
   A. Read the title and headings
   B. Close the book
   C. Read every word carefully
   D. Skip the page

10. What is skimming? (1 mark)
   A. Reading quickly to get the main idea
   B. Reading backwards
   C. Reading slowly for every word
   D. Copying the text

11. What is animal welfare? (1 mark)
   A. Hunting animals
   B. Ignoring animals
   C. Taking good care of animals so they are healthy and safe
   D. Selling animals only

12. Why should you mark pauses in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. To spoil the page
   B. To hide words
   C. To make it longer
   D. To know where to stop and breathe

13. How should you read a sad poem? (1 mark)
   A. Laughing
   B. Without a pause
   C. Slowly and softly
   D. Fast and loudly

14. What is the meaning of reciting a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Erasing it
   B. Copying it
   C. Saying it aloud, usually from memory
   D. Writing it

15. Why are stories important in communities? (1 mark)
   A. They teach values and keep history
   B. They hide the truth
   C. They waste time
   D. They cause trouble

16. What does a picture story use? (1 mark)
   A. Pictures showing the beginning, middle and end
   B. Only maps
   C. Only numbers
   D. Only names

17. What is the problem in a story? (1 mark)
   A. The page
   B. The title
   C. The ending word
   D. The trouble or challenge the characters face

18. Why should you not invent interjections for your mother tongue? (1 mark)
   A. It is easy to invent them correctly
   B. Nobody uses them
   C. They are learned from speakers of the language
   D. Languages have no interjections

19. What is a motion in a debate? (1 mark)
   A. A song
   B. A dance
   C. The statement the teams discuss
   D. A gift

20. In the kite passage, what went wrong? (1 mark)
   A. The kite flew away forever
   B. The children fell
   C. The wind stopped
   D. The string broke

21. Which interjection shows sudden understanding? (1 mark)
   A. Yuck
   B. Oops
   C. Ouch
   D. Aha

22. In a script dialogue, what comes straight after the speaker's name? (1 mark)
   A. A full stop
   B. A number
   C. A bracket
   D. A colon

23. What is good telephone manner? (1 mark)
   A. Interrupting
   B. Calling very late for no reason
   C. Speaking with food in your mouth
   D. Speaking clearly and giving your name

24. What is a headline? (1 mark)
   A. A picture
   B. A short eye-catching title
   C. The last word
   D. A price

25. Why should you write true information on a form? (1 mark)
   A. False answers are best
   B. It is a game
   C. Forms are records and false information causes problems
   D. Nobody reads forms

26. What does turn taking mean? (1 mark)
   A. Speaking all at once
   B. Speaking one at a time and waiting for your chance
   C. Refusing to speak
   D. Speaking loudest

27. What is a good leader described as in the model poem? (1 mark)
   A. Angry
   B. Rude
   C. Fair and kind
   D. Lazy

28. What should you use in your answers to poem questions? (1 mark)
   A. Your favourite song
   B. Words from the poem
   C. A dictionary only
   D. Nothing

29. What is an instruction chart? (1 mark)
   A. A drawing of a house
   B. A poster showing steps for a task
   C. A story chart
   D. A list of animals

30. Which is a verb in Open your book? (1 mark)
   A. the
   B. Open
   C. book
   D. your

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write a short paragraph of three sentences about today's weather. Use at least one comma in a list, two capital letters for names and three full stops. (5 marks)

32. Explain the steps of organising a class debate. (4 marks)

33. Write the plural of each English noun: plate, tomato. (2 marks)

34. Give three rules for punctuating a dialogue. (3 marks)

35. State three steps for reading your part in a dialogue. (3 marks)

36. After listening to a safety story, describe how you would answer four kinds of comprehension questions and give one example of each. (5 marks)

37. Explain what a subject and a predicate are, then write one sentence and divide it. (5 marks)

38. Explain the difference in punctuation between Wow! and Oops, it is torn. (3 marks)

39. List three steps for understanding a poem. (3 marks)

40. Write a five-sentence oral paragraph about a free day. Include three interjections that show different feelings. (5 marks)

41. Explain what attentive listening means. (2 marks)

42. Name three ways to practise letter shapes before writing them. (3 marks)

43. Explain what the proverb Many hands make light work means. (2 marks)

44. Write one correct line of a dialogue with a speaker name and an interjection. (2 marks)

45. Name three parts of a simple form. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Bring
   Bring shows the action.

2. A — In a simple dictionary
   Dictionaries give meanings.

3. C — A comma
   We usually put a comma after First at the start of a sentence.

4. A — The classroom was a beehive.
   A metaphor says one thing is another.

5. A — She is as bright as the sun.
   It uses as to compare.

6. D — It is fast and does not disturb others
   Silent reading is quiet and lets you think.

7. C — To show we understand the lesson
   Explaining shows understanding of the meaning.

8. B — Clearly and with feeling
   Clear speech and feeling make a story good.

9. A — Read the title and headings
   The title tells the topic.

10. A — Reading quickly to get the main idea
   Skimming gives the general idea.

11. C — Taking good care of animals so they are healthy and safe
   Welfare means care for animals' well-being.

12. D — To know where to stop and breathe
   Pauses help the listener follow.

13. C — Slowly and softly
   Slow and soft matches sadness.

14. C — Saying it aloud, usually from memory
   To recite is to say aloud.

15. A — They teach values and keep history
   Stories teach and entertain.

16. A — Pictures showing the beginning, middle and end
   A picture story tells events with drawings.

17. D — The trouble or challenge the characters face
   The problem drives the events.

18. C — They are learned from speakers of the language
   Ask real speakers for correct forms.

19. C — The statement the teams discuss
   The motion is the topic.

20. D — The string broke
   The string broke and the kite fell.

21. D — Aha
   Aha shows realising something.

22. D — A colon
   The name is followed by a colon.

23. D — Speaking clearly and giving your name
   Clarity and courtesy help.

24. B — A short eye-catching title
   A headline is the title of an advert or news item.

25. C — Forms are records and false information causes problems
   Honest answers are important.

26. B — Speaking one at a time and waiting for your chance
   Turn taking is orderly speaking.

27. C — Fair and kind
   The poem advises fairness and kindness.

28. B — Words from the poem
   Answers should come from the poem.

29. B — A poster showing steps for a task
   It shows steps in order.

30. B — Open
   Open is the action.

SECTION B
----
31. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any three correct sentences, for example On Monday in Kisumu the sky was cloudy. It was cool, windy and dry. Amina wore a sweater.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence that is complete and correct, one for a comma in a list and one for correct capitals.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a motion, form two teams, plan reasons, take turns to speak for about a minute each, listeners note points, the class votes.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: plates, tomatoes
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct plural.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Name then colon, capital letter to begin the words, end with a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark, a new line for each speaker.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read silently first, underline your lines, practise them, watch the punctuation, wait for your cue.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: Answer who with a person (his mother), what with an event (touched the pot), where with a place (the clinic) and why with a reason (he wanted to see the steam). Give short, full answers and ask for repetition if needed.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each kind and example, and one mark for full sentences.

37. (5 marks)
   Answer: The subject is who or what the sentence is about and the predicate says what the subject does. Example: The girl (subject) counts the coins (predicate).
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the two meanings, one for a sentence, and two marks for the correct division.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: An exclamation mark shows strong feeling, and a comma after a mild interjection shows a softer feeling.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each punctuation mark and one for the difference.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read the title, read it aloud more than once, find meanings of new words, say the message in your own words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

40. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any five sentences with three suitable interjections such as Hurray, Wow and Oops used to show joy, surprise and a mistake.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence and one mark for three suitable interjections shown correctly.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Attentive listening means choosing to give your eyes, ears and mind to the speaker so that you understand and remember what is said.
   Working / marking points: One mark for choosing to pay attention and one mark for understanding or remembering.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Trace in the air, trace on a card, model with clay or string, paint them.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each way.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: When people share a task, the work becomes easier and faster.
   Working / marking points: One mark for sharing work and one for easier work.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Neema: Wow! The sun is shining.
   Working / marking points: One mark for name with colon and one for an interjection.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Title, instructions, fields, signature, date.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.
